The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs nothing and puts you in touch with someone who can review what happened and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives injured people two years from the date of an accident to file a personal injury claim. Claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still pursue compensation — it's simply reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you pay nothing upfront and owe no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Live Oak?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your injury involved a government entity, such as a city road crew, the notice window can be as short as six months. It's wise to act sooner rather than later so evidence and records stay available.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Live Oak?
items.answer: Public collision records show that reported injury crashes in Live Oak are concentrated along corridors such as Rt 99, Pennington Road, and Larkin Road, with reports also clustering on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral public-record patterns, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. Certain specialized cases, such as medical malpractice, can have different rules, which an attorney can explain.

items.question: What does it cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so you owe no fee unless they recover compensation for you.
